mainTopic: When a person is liable for both money and מלקות: does he pay or get lashes? (עולא vs. רבי יוחנן)
overview: The גמרא is settling a clash: our משנה says a man who violates his sister pays a קנס, but the משנה in מכות says he gets מלקות. עולא holds that when both money and lashes apply, a person pays and is not flogged, and he learns this from the word 'תחת' in the rape פסוק and in 'עין תחת עין'. רבי יוחנן answers differently: one משנה is where he was warned (התראה) and gets lashes, the other is where he was not warned and pays. So רבי יוחנן holds that with a warning, lashes win over money, and he learns it from 'כדי רשעתו' placed next to 'ארבעים יכנו'. The גמרא challenges him from חובל בחבירו, since his own ruling shows that a warned injurer who causes real damage pays. The answer, using רבי אילעא's principle, is that the Torah explicitly singled out the injurer for payment, just as it did for עדים זוממין. The גמרא traces רבי אילעא's statement to a מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and חכמים about false witnesses, and shows the extra words 'יד ביד' and 'כן ינתן בו' both point to money. Finally, רבי יוחנן rejects עולא's rule, because it would cancel the lashes for ערות אחותך.

steps.title: עולא's source: the word 'תחת' links rape to injury
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns his rule from a גזירה שוה between 'תחת אשר ענה' (rape) and 'עין תחת עין' (injury). For injury, a person pays and is not flogged. So in any case of money plus lashes, he pays and is not flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עולא learns it from the word 'תחת' appearing in two places. Here it says 'because (תחת) he afflicted her.' There it says 'an eye for (תחת) an eye.' There, for injury, he pays money and is not flogged. So too, anywhere there is both money and lashes, he pays money and is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: An earlier try at finding עולא's source did not work. Now the גמרא gives him a new source: a word-link between two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'תחת' appears in the rape פסוק and in the injury פסוק. Injury law is known to be money, not lashes. That pattern gets carried over to rape, and to every case where both punishments could apply.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In place of' or 'because of'. The shared word used for the link
He learns it out (here, through a גזירה שוה)

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: money plus lashes means he pays and is not flogged. His source is the גזירה שוה of 'תחת' and 'תחת'.

phrases.english: Rather, עולא learns it from 'for' (תחת) and 'for' (תחת).
It is written here: 'because he afflicted her,'
and it is written there: 'an eye for an eye.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה הָתָם — מָמוֹנָא מְשַׁלֵּם, מִילְקָא לָא לָקֵי;
phrases.english: Just as there, he pays money and is not flogged;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מָמוֹנָא וּמַלְקוֹת —
phrases.english: so too, anywhere there is both money and lashes,
he pays money and is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces an earlier rejected source for עולא's rule (from before this section).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier source could not support עולא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'תחת/תחת' link proves that money takes priority over lashes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the difference is whether he was warned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן settles the contradiction differently. Both משניות can be about a sister who is a נערה. מכות is where he was warned, so he gets lashes. Our משנה is where he was not warned, so he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even if you say both are about his sister who is a נערה, there is no problem. There, he was warned. Here, he was not warned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new way to settle the clash between our משנה (he pays) and the משנה in מכות (he gets lashes). The key is whether witnesses warned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to say the two משניות are about different girls. Same girl, same sin. The only difference is התראה. Without a warning lashes are impossible, so he pays the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Even if you say'. Introduces a broader answer
His sister who is a young girl (age of the קנס)
They warned him (התראה), which is needed before lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two 'כאן' rows. The first 'כאן' (warned) is the משנה in מכות, with lashes. The second 'כאן' (not warned) is our משנה, with payment.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
Even if you say it is his sister who is a young girl,
there, they warned him;
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מכות, where he gets lashes.

phrases.english: here, they did not warn him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא אֲחוֹתוֹ נַעֲרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction than עולא's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (warned vs. not warned)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to clash about the same sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Warned means lashes. Not warned means payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lashes apply when he was warned. Payment applies when he was not.

steps.title: What רבי יוחנן must hold: warned means lashes, not money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יוחנן's answer. He must hold that in any money-plus-lashes case with a warning, the person gets lashes and does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems רבי יוחנן holds: anywhere there is both money and lashes, and they warned him, he gets lashes and does not pay money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls a general rule out of רבי יוחנן's answer. This sets up the next question about where he gets it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's answer is the opposite of עולא's rule. עולא says money always wins. רבי יוחנן says that once there is a warning, lashes win.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So it seems'. Introduces a conclusion drawn from what was said
They warned him (Aramaic for הִתְרוּ בּוֹ)

phrases.english: So it seems רבי יוחנן holds:
anywhere there is both money and lashes
and they warned him,
he gets lashes and does not pay money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle out of רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money plus lashes with a warning means lashes and no payment.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוחנן learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוחנן's principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does רבי יוחנן get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source supports the rule it just found in רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that lashes win over money needs a פסוק behind it. This is especially true since עולא brought a פסוק for the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where does he know it?'. A request for a source

phrases.english: From where does רבי יוחנן derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the principle drawn in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for 'warned means lashes, not money'.

steps.title: Source: 'כדי רשעתו' next to 'ארבעים יכנו'
steps.stepSummary: 'כדי רשעתו' teaches that he is punished for only one wickedness, not two. The next פסוק, 'ארבעים יכנו', shows that the one punishment is lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'according to his wickedness.' You make him liable for one wickedness, but not for two. And right next to it: 'Forty lashes he shall give him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two פסוקים that sit side by side. One says to give only one punishment. The other shows that the punishment is lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'רשעתו' is singular, so only one punishment can be given. Since the lashes פסוק comes right after it, the one punishment chosen is lashes, not money.

keyTerms.meaning: And right next to it, a lesson learned from the closeness of two פסוקים

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two opposite rules. עולא says money wins. רבי יוחנן says that with a warning, lashes win.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'according to his wickedness,'
for one wickedness you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁתֵּי רִשְׁעָיוֹת.
phrases.english: but you do not make him liable for two wickednesses.
And next to it: 'Forty he shall strike him.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כדי רשעתו' means one punishment only, and the closeness of 'ארבעים יכנו' shows it is lashes.

steps.title: Challenge: an injurer pays and is not flogged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from חובל בחבירו. There, both money and lashes apply, yet the injurer pays and is not flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about one who injures his fellow? There is both money and lashes there, yet he pays money and is not flogged!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's principle with the case of someone who injures another person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting someone breaks a לאו, so lashes could apply, and it also causes damage that must be paid. The known law is that he pays. That seems to go against 'lashes win'.

phrases.english: But what about one who injures his fellow,
where there is both money and lashes,
he pays money and is not flogged!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle just given a source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's principle that lashes win when there is a warning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the injury case, money is paid even though lashes are possible.

steps.title: Possible defense: the injurer pays only when not warned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests an answer. Maybe the injurer pays only when he was not warned, but with a warning he gets lashes and does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: that applies only when they did not warn him, but if they warned him he gets lashes and does not pay money...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to save רבי יוחנן. It does this only to knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This applies the same warned/not-warned split from step 2 to the injury case. If it held up, the challenge would disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say'. A suggested answer the גמרא will reject
'These words apply' only in a certain case

phrases.english: And if you say:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: this applies only where they did not warn him,
but if they warned him,
he gets lashes and does not pay money,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a defense against the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The injurer always pays, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe the injurer pays only when he was not warned.

steps.title: Rebuttal: רבי יוחנן's own ruling about a blow worth less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with רבי יוחנן's own ruling, said in his name by רבי אמי. A blow causing less than a שוה פרוטה of damage earns lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אמי say in the name of רבי יוחנן: if he struck him a blow that does not cause a פרוטה's worth of damage, he gets lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רבי יוחנן himself to knock down the defense of step 7. The next step will explain why it shows that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says lashes are given only when the damage is less than a פרוטה. That suggests that when there is real damage, he pays instead, even with a warning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But didn't he say?'. Brings a source against an idea
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as money

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: but didn't רבי אמי say that רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: הִכָּהוּ הַכָּאָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה — לוֹקֶה.
phrases.english: if he struck him a blow that is not worth a פרוטה, he is flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense of step 7 using רבי יוחנן's own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that a warned injurer gets lashes instead of paying
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן limits lashes to blows worth less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: Working it out: even when warned, real damage means payment
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's case must involve a warning, since lashes need one. So the only reason for lashes is that the damage is less than a פרוטה. With real damage, he would pay and not be flogged, even when warned. That goes against רבי יוחנן's principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If they did not warn him, why is he flogged? So it must be that they warned him. And the reason he is flogged is that the damage is less than a פרוטה. But if it were worth a פרוטה, he would pay money and not be flogged!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן's ruling about a small blow knocks down the defense. This completes the challenge against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes always need a warning, so his case must be a warned one. Since 'less than a פרוטה' is the stated reason for lashes, it follows that real damage brings payment instead, warning or not. This clashes with 'warned means lashes'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the case?'. Pinning down the facts
But if there is (worth). Reading the rule the other way around

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge against רבי יוחנן: by his own ruling, a warned injurer who causes a פרוטה's worth of damage pays and is not flogged. That does not fit 'warned means lashes, not money'.

phrases.english: What is the case?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ, אַמַּאי לוֹקֶה?
phrases.english: If they did not warn him, why is he flogged?
Rather, obviously they warned him,
and the reason is that it is not worth a פרוטה,
but if it is worth a פרוטה,
he pays money and is not flogged!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ, אַמַּאי לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how step 8's ruling disproves the defense, completing the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That a warned injurer who causes real damage pays and is not flogged
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אמי quoting רבי יוחנן about a blow worth less than a פרוטה

steps.title: The Torah made a special exception for the injurer
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי אילעא's principle, the גמרא answers that the Torah explicitly singled out חובל בחבירו for payment, just as it did for עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אילעא said: the Torah explicitly added payment for false witnesses. Here too, the Torah explicitly added payment for someone who injures another person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 9. The injurer pays because the Torah made a special exception for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's general rule still stands: when both lashes and money apply and he was warned, he gets lashes. חובל בחבירו is an exception, because the Torah clearly says he pays. The same kind of exception exists for עדים זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah added or included (a case)
Plotting false witnesses, proven false by other witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי יוחנן's principle. It turns the case of the injurer into a special exception instead of a disproof.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ile'a said:
The Torah explicitly included
conspiring witnesses for payment,
here too:
the Torah explicitly included
one who injures another for payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in Steps 6–9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The injurer paying even with a warning seemed to disprove רבי יוחנן's rule of lashes over money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The injurer is a special case. The Torah explicitly made him pay, so the general rule does not apply to him.

steps.title: Where did רבי אילעא say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי אילעא's statement was originally said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was רבי אילעא's statement said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the original setting of רבי אילעא's teaching. This sets up the next step, which quotes that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing where a statement came from shows what it originally meant. This lets us see that it really fits the injurer's case too.

phrases.english: And where was the statement of Rabbi Ile'a said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the principle used in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original setting of רבי אילעא's statement.

steps.title: False witnesses about a debt: רבי מאיר and חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The statement was said about false witnesses who claimed someone owes 200 זוז. רבי מאיר says they get lashes and pay; חכמים say whoever pays is not flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said about this case. Witnesses said: we testify that this man owes his friend 200 זוז. They were then proven to be plotting false witnesses. They get lashes and also pay, because the source that makes them get lashes is not the source that makes them pay. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: anyone who pays does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the case where רבי אילעא's statement belongs. It is a מחלוקת about false witnesses who tried to make someone pay money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives both punishments, because each comes from a different פסוק. חכמים give only one punishment, and it is payment. That one detail, why payment and not lashes, is what רבי אילעא comes to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: They were proven to be plotting false witnesses
They get lashes and also pay
The source, the reason or פסוק behind a punishment

steps.confusionAlert: חכמים here say 'whoever pays is not flogged.' That sounds like עולא's general rule. But as the next steps show, the reason payment wins here is the Torah's special signal for עדים זוממין ('יד ביד', step 16).

phrases.english: On this:
"We testify about so-and-so
that he owes his fellow two hundred zuz,"
and they were found to be conspiring witnesses —
they are flogged and they pay,
because the source that brings them to lashes
phrases.notes: Lashes come from the ban on false testimony, and payment from 'do to him as he plotted.' They are two separate sources.

phrases.english: is not what brings them to payment,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
Anyone who pays is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 by quoting the source case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement belongs to the מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and חכמים about עדים זוממין who testified about a money debt.

steps.title: Why not say lashes win instead?
steps.stepSummary: On the חכמים's view, the גמרא challenges: why not say the opposite, that whoever gets lashes does not pay?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say instead: anyone who gets lashes does not pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים. If only one punishment applies, why should it be payment rather than lashes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only one punishment is given, nothing so far shows why it should be payment rather than lashes. The opposite rule, 'whoever is flogged does not pay', sounds just as reasonable. So the חכמים need a reason to choose money, and this question is what drew out רבי אילעא's statement.

phrases.english: But let us say: anyone who is flogged does not pay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of חכמים quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: חכמים's ruling that payment, not lashes, is the punishment for עדים זוממין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only one punishment applies, nothing so far shows why it should be money and not lashes.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: the Torah chose payment for false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא answers that the Torah explicitly included false witnesses for payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: the Torah explicitly included false witnesses for payment.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is רבי אילעא's statement in its original place. It answers why the חכמים pick payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a clear Torah signal that false witnesses pay. That is why, when only one punishment is given, it is payment and not lashes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:
The Torah explicitly included
conspiring witnesses for payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא: בְּפֵירוּשׁ רִיבְּתָה תּוֹרָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lashes might be the one punishment instead of payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: For עדים זוממין, the Torah clearly points to money, so they pay and are not flogged.

steps.title: Where does the Torah say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the Torah this explicit inclusion is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did the Torah include this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the actual פסוק behind רבי אילעא's claim. The next step will show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A claim that the Torah 'explicitly' said something needs a text to back it up. The גמרא is asking for that text.

phrases.english: Where did the Torah include this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the claim in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that עדים זוממין pay money.

steps.title: 'Hand for hand' means money
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah already said 'do to him as he plotted,' the extra words 'יד ביד' teach something passed from hand to hand, which is money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah already wrote: 'You shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother.' Why do I need 'hand for hand'? It means something given from hand to hand. What is that? Money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source. The extra words 'יד ביד' point to money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general punishment for false witnesses was already stated. So 'יד ביד' must be adding something. Something handed from one hand to another is money, so the Torah is pointing to payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (signals extra words that teach something)

phrases.english: Now, since it is written:
"And you shall do to him as he plotted
to do to his brother,"
why do I need "hand for hand"?
Something that is given from hand to hand,
and what is that? Money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי כְּתִיב: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'יד ביד' teach something passed hand to hand, which is money.

steps.title: 'So shall be given' means money for the injurer
steps.stepSummary: The same reasoning works for חובל בחבירו. The extra words 'כן ינתן בו' point to giving, which is money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to one who injures another. The Torah already wrote: 'As he did, so shall be done to him.' Why do I need 'so shall be given to him'? It means something that involves giving. What is that? Money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim from Step 10 that the Torah explicitly made the injurer pay. It uses the same style of reading as for false witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כן יעשה לו' already gave the punishment. So the extra word 'ינתן', 'shall be given', must teach something. Giving points to money. That is why the injurer pays instead of getting lashes, without breaking רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule (lashes, not money) has two Torah-made exceptions. עדים זוממין pay because of 'יד ביד', and חובל בחבירו pays because of 'כן ינתן בו'.

phrases.english: One who injures another too:
Now, since it is written:
"As he has done, so shall be done to him,"
why do I need "so shall be given to him"?
Something that involves giving,
and what is that? Money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the derivation from Step 16 to the injurer, backing up Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah explicitly made חובל בחבירו pay money.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יוחנן hold like עולא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן does not agree with עולא, who says that when both apply, one pays and is not flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן: what is the reason he did not say like עולא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן rejects עולא's approach. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have just seen two cases where payment wins. One might think that is simply the general rule, as עולא says. The גמרא wants to know why רבי יוחנן treats them only as exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: עולא, the אמורא who holds that payment wins over lashes

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan:
What is the reason he did not say like Ulla?
phrases.notes: עולא's view, stated earlier on this page, is that when money and lashes both apply, he pays and is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the exceptions to why רבי יוחנן rejects עולא's general rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן does not accept that payment always takes priority over lashes.

steps.title: Otherwise the lashes for ערות אחותך would be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: If payment always won, the lashes for the איסור of ערות אחותך would be cancelled in the case where a קנס applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, you would cancel 'You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: עולא's rule would wipe out the lashes for the איסור with one's sister in the case where he also owes money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who sins with his sister can also owe a קנס. If payment always pushed away lashes, the usual lashes for this איסור would not be given there. רבי יוחנן will not let that איסור lose its lashes, so he says lashes win.

keyTerms.meaning: You have cancelled, made it pointless
The ban on relations with one's sister

phrases.english: If so,
you have cancelled "The nakedness of your sister... you shall not uncover."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:9. He means the lashes for this איסור would never be given in this case, since he would only pay.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולא's rule would cancel the lashes of the איסור ערות אחותך wherever a קנס is also owed.
